security_audit.summary: AI review confirmed critical pipe-to-shell installer instructions and high-risk local binary installation guidance. Most API-key and Markdown backtick detections are documentation placeholders or command examples, but the skill still directs agents to run a networked CLI. Semantic review also found explicit local file uploads and Twitter/X automation that require strong user consent.

remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell examples with verified release downloads, checksum validation, and explicit user confirmation before installation.
Document provenance, signature verification, and removal steps before moving downloaded binaries into ~/.local/bin.
Require explicit approval for each upload, warn about sensitive paths, and recommend limiting uploads to intended assets.
Require explicit confirmation before posts, DMs, follows, likes, or retweets, and show the exact account action.
Tell users that prompts and files are sent to external apps and may incur cost or quota usage.

content.user_title: Run AI Apps from the Command Line
content.value_statement: Teams often need one interface for cloud AI apps without managing GPUs or separate SDKs. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through the inference.sh CLI workflow.
actual_capabilities: Installs and authenticates the belt CLI for inference.sh workflows.
Finds public AI apps by category, search term, featured status, or recency.
Runs image, video, text, search, 3D, and Twitter/X apps from CLI commands.
Generates sample inputs, inspects app schemas, and runs tasks with inline or file input.
Tracks long-running tasks and retrieves saved outputs from completed jobs.
Explains local file upload behavior for media inputs.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh account, belt CLI access, and available account credits.
Inputs, prompts, and selected local files may be sent to external cloud apps.
It does not verify app trust, output accuracy, pricing, or quota impact.
Social media actions require account authorization and careful human approval.

use_cases.title: Prototype multimodal AI features
use_cases.description: Run image, video, speech, search, and LLM apps from one CLI during product exploration.

use_cases.title: Create media assets quickly
use_cases.description: Generate images, videos, avatars, audio, or 3D assets without local GPU setup.

use_cases.title: Automate model operations
use_cases.description: Discover apps, generate sample inputs, run tasks, and retrieve outputs from repeatable shell workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Find an app
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to find inference.sh apps for image generation. Show the most relevant options and explain when to use each one.

prompt_templates.title: Run a simple task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to run a cloud AI app for my prompt. Ask before sending data to the external service.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a media workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to prepare a video generation workflow from my local image. Confirm the exact file before uploading it.

prompt_templates.title: Build a repeatable pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to design a repeatable CLI workflow that discovers an app, creates sample input, runs it, and checks task results.

output_examples.input: Find an app for high quality image generation.
output_examples.output: A short recommendation list with app names, categories, strengths, and a suggested next command sequence.

output_examples.input: Run a video generation task and check the result later.
output_examples.output: A workflow outline that creates input, submits the task without waiting, records the task ID, and checks completion.

output_examples.input: Use a local image as the source for an avatar video.
output_examples.output: A consent-first checklist that confirms the file path, explains upload behavior, and prepares the app run steps.

best_practices: Confirm every external command before running it, especially installers and account-changing actions.
Inspect app schemas and sample inputs before sending prompts, files, or credentials.
Use version pinning and record task IDs for repeatable, auditable workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installers directly into a shell without independent verification.
Do not upload local files until the user confirms the exact path and purpose.
Do not automate posts, DMs, likes, follows, or retweets without explicit approval.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use the inference.sh belt CLI to discover and run cloud AI apps.

faq.question: Do I need an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow requires belt CLI access, authentication, and available account credits for paid or quota-limited apps.

faq.question: Can it use local files?
faq.answer: Yes. The referenced CLI can upload local files when a path is supplied, so confirm every file before use.

faq.question: Can it automate Twitter or X?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill lists posting and account actions, so every action should require clear human approval first.

faq.question: Does it run models locally?
faq.answer: No. It runs apps through the inference.sh cloud service and returns task results or hosted output links.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: The main concerns are remote installer execution, local file uploads, external app execution, and social media account actions.
